title: Microcanonical Operator Spectrum, BPS Chaos and Free Probability Theory
authors: Alexandre Belin, Yichao Fu, Federico La Rocca
abstract: Matrix elements of simple operators are central to thermalization in chaotic quantum many-body systems. Their moments are often described statistically through the Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis. In this paper, we study a more refined characterization of these matrix elements: the eigenspectrum of simple operators once projected to microcanonical energy windows. The spectrum encodes all moments of the matrix elements at once, and is particularly relevant when the spectrum of the Hamiltonian is degenerate. Assuming that the eigenbasis of the simple operator is Haar-randomly oriented with respect to that of the Hamiltonian, we prove that the spectrum of an operator projected to a small microcanonical window obeys Gaussian random matrix statistics. We do this directly by studying the probability distribution inherited from the random orientation, as well as using tools from Free Probability Theory. We discuss the implications for BPS chaos and more generally for eigenstate thermalization.
summary: This theoretical paper studies the eigenvalue statistics of an operator projected onto a specific energy window in a chaotic quantum system. By assuming random eigenbasis orientation, the authors prove that these statistics follow Gaussian Random Matrix Theory predictions. This provides a powerful, refined diagnostic tool for understanding quantum thermalization beyond standard two-point correlation functions.
main_problem: The paper investigates a refined diagnostic for thermalization in chaotic quantum systems: the eigenspectrum of a simple operator projected onto microcanonical energy windows.
main_result: Under the assumption of random eigenbasis orientation, the spectrum of this projected operator is shown to obey Gaussian random matrix statistics (GUE) to quadratic order in the projection parameter.
method: The analysis employs tools from Free Probability Theory and relies on calculating the joint probability density of the eigenvalues of the projected operator.
model_or_system: The system is a chaotic quantum many-body system where an operator $O$ is projected onto a microcanonical subspace defined by a projector $P_K$. The analysis is performed in the large $N$ limit.
key_observables: The joint probability density of the eigenvalues $\mu(\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_K)$, the one-point eigenvalue distribution $ho(\lambda)$, and the two-point correlation function.
important_parameters: The projection parameter $\alpha = K/N$, and the size of the system $N$ (in the large $N$ limit).
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that the eigenbasis of the simple operator is Haar-randomly oriented with respect to the Hamiltonian's eigenbasis.
figures_summary: The figures compare numerical results against theoretical predictions for eigenvalue statistics (level density, spacing, SFF) across varying projection parameters $\alpha$, showing deviations from GUE as $\alpha$ increases.
paper_structure: The paper sets up the problem by defining the projected operator $O_K$, derives the joint probability density using complex integrals (HCIZ), and then discusses the results using both direct calculation and the complementary framework of Free Probability Theory.
why_interesting: The connection between spectral statistics (RMT/GUE) and thermalization diagnostics (ETH) is fundamental to understanding quantum dynamics in complex systems, which is a key area for AMO physics.
